subject: Request: adjusted availability minimums & monthly remedy model
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@stellarbank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarbank.com, ops@stellarbank.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: adjusted availability minimums & monthly remedy model

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week — StellarBank is excited about Redwood's performance. As we move toward procurement, our security and procurement teams have asked us to request a tighter availability & remedy profile for the hosted endpoints that will be critical to our fraud-detection flows. We have two asks we'd like you to review:

1) Availability minimums: we need a guaranteed hosted availability floor of 99.95% for production endpoints used by real-time fraud scoring. For batched scoring jobs (nightly reconciliation) we understand latency is looser but would like a defined SLA floor as well.

2) Remedy model: Rather than a single step credit, our finance team prefers a pro-rata monthly credit model tied to % availability shortfall, with an overall cap at no less than 50% of the monthly recurring fees (we can detail accounting practices). We also want to ensure maintenance carveouts are explicit and that scheduled maintenance windows cannot exceed X hours/month without renegotiation.

Attached is a short doc with our requested language and examples (StellarBank_SLA_asks_v1.docx). Can Redwood share a redline or counter that identifies where you'd accept exceptions and where you cannot? Also curious about latency SLOs for p95 on the real-time endpoints — our target is <= 250ms p95.

Nina Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, StellarBank
N: 415-555-0192
[Attachment: StellarBank_SLA_asks_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@stellarbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: adjusted availability minimums & monthly remedy model

Hi Nina — really appreciate the clear asks and the doc. Glad StellarBank liked the demo. I'll outline Redwood's initial position below and follow up with a clean PDF proposal.

Quick summary of our counter-proposal (high level):
- Hosted availability: standard is 99.95% for single-region hosted deployments. We can commit to 99.95% for your production real-time endpoints. For batched reconciliation jobs we propose a separate line in the SLA with a 99.5% floor given the different workload characteristics.
- Latency: for real-time endpoints we aim for p95 <= 300ms for our hosted tier; we can discuss an operational plan to hit 250ms but would need traffic pattern data and to evaluate request distribution. Batched endpoints would have a p95 target of 400ms.
- Remedy model: we do not typically do strictly pro-rata credits tied to minute-by-minute availability (that creates unpredictable billing complexity), but we can offer a tiered monthly credit ladder that scales with the availability shortfall and a monthly cap. As an initial offer: small shortfalls -> 10% credit, medium -> 30%, severe -> 60%, with an overall cap at 50% of the monthly fee (we're open to refinement).

I attached a short PDF with the initial redline and a sample credit table (SB-proposal-20250729.pdf). Before I loop legal, can you confirm your stickiest items (availability floor vs latency target vs cap)? If 250ms p95 on real-time is non-negotiable we can explore a dedicated capacity carveout (dedicated pools), which changes the economics.

I'll loop Marissa (our Head of Renewals) and Ben (legal lead on remedies) for contract language.

Best,
Logan Wright
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 206-555-0123
[Attachment: SB-proposal-20250729.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 17:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: adjusted availability minimums & monthly remedy model

Marissa / Ben — forwarding StellarBank's asks. Key points: 99.95% hosted availability ask, 250ms p95 target for real-time, and a request for a pro-rata monthly credit model with a suggested cap at 50% of MRR.

My suggested approach: offer 99.95% hosted, batched 99.5%, latency p95 real-time 300ms (but include a mechanism: if Stellar provides traffic patterns and we can validate with a 30-day test we will commit to 250ms and then transition to dedicated or higher-resourced pools if not met). For credits, propose the tiered ladder (10/30/60) with monthly cap at 50% but the legal team should consider adding a remediation escrow and an exception for scheduled maintenance up to 8 hours/month (anything above is creditable).

Marissa — can you draft the public-facing ladder language and confirm the monthly cap we can accept commercially? Ben — please flag any legal risk with the escrow/measurement approach.

Thanks,
Logan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@stellarbank.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, logan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: adjusted availability minimums & monthly remedy model

Hi Nina — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Below is Redwood's proposed amendment that we think is commercially reasonable while addressing StellarBank's needs. I've attached a redline you can review and sign.

Key proposal (redwood counter):
- Availability: Hosted production real-time endpoints: 99.95% monthly uptime. Batched reconciliation endpoints: 99.5% monthly uptime.
- Latency (p95): Real-time endpoints: 300ms target; if StellarBank provides 30 days of representative traffic and Redwood validates an operational plan we will commit to 250ms p95 for the production slice listed in Appendix A (this may require a phased capacity commitment or moving to a Dedicated pool). Batched endpoints: 400ms p95.
- Remedy ladder (monthly credits applied to recurring fees):
  * 99.95% - 99.50% => 10% credit
  * 99.49% - 99.00% => 30% credit
  * < 99.00% => 60% credit
- Monthly cap: 50% of monthly recurring fees.
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance (>=48h notice) up to 8 hours/month is excluded from uptime calculation. Unscheduled maintenance or emergency remediation is creditable per the ladder.

We are also proposing a quarterly SLA review between StellarBank and Redwood to iterate on targets and traffic assumptions. If those terms look acceptable to you, I'll issue a DocuSign-ready amendment (see link) and Ben will add the measurement/monitoring text for how uptime is calculated (region-level metrics, p95 calculation method, and data retention for audit).

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/sign/SB-2025-042
Drive: https://redwood.app/drive/SB-2025-042/sla-draft

Attachments: SLA-amendment-redwood-20250730.pdf (contains full redline and Appendix A sample traffic slice)

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0178

From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@stellarbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@stellarbank.com, ops@stellarbank.com, logan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: adjusted availability minimums & monthly remedy model

Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity. StellarBank can accept the availability floors and the tiered ladder as written, conditioned on two items before we sign:

1) Latency: we need the real-time p95 committed at 250ms (not conditioned on the 30-day test). We're willing to commit to a 3-month pilot window during which we provide traffic patterns and run a joint ops test; if Redwood misses the 250ms p95 during the pilot, we accept the proposed mechanism to move to a Dedicated pool with adjusted pricing.

2) Quarterly SLA review: include explicit language about what will be reviewed (traffic quantiles, tail latency, and error rates) and an ability to rebaseline targets with 60 days' notice.

If you put those two items into the amendment text, we can sign via DocuSign this week.

Nina Patel
Senior Procurement Manager, StellarBank
